==English==
{{wp|<dab!>}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|rāt}}, {{IPA|en|/ɹeɪt/|a=RP,GA}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-rate.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|eɪt|s=1}}

===Etymology 1===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂er-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|rate}}, from {{der|en|fro|rate}}, from {{der|en|la-med|rata}}, from {{der|en|la||prō ratā parte|according to a fixed part}}, from {{m|la|ratus||fixed}}, from {{m|la|reor|rērī|think, deem, judge, estimate", ''originally'' "reckon, calculate}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{lb|en|obsolete}} The [[worth]] of something; [[value]]. {{defdate|15th|19th centuries}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Romeo and Juliet|V|3|text=There shall no figure at such '''rate''' be set, / As that of true and faithfull Iuliet.}}
#* {{RQ:Fielding Tom Jones|text=His natural parts were not of the first '''rate''', but he had greatly improved them by a learned education.}}
# The [[proportional]] [[relationship]] between one [[amount]], value etc. and another. {{defdate|from 15th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|At the height of his powers, he was producing pictures at the '''rate''' of four a year.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|title=No hiding place| date=2013-05-25| volume=407| issue=8837| page=74| url=http://www.economist.com/news/science-and-technology/21578357-plan-assess-peoples-personal-characteristics-their-twitter-streams-no| passage=In America alone, people spent $170 billion on “direct marketing”—junk mail of both the physical and electronic varieties—last year. Yet of those who received unsolicited adverts through the post, only 3% bought anything as a result. If the bumf arrived electronically, the take-up '''rate''' was 0.1%. And for online adverts the “conversion” into sales was a minuscule 0.01%.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20171025020559/https://www.economist.com/news/science-and-technology/21578357-plan-assess-peoples-personal-characteristics-their-twitter-streams-no|archivedate=25 October 2017}}
# [[speed|Speed]]. {{defdate|from 17th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|The car was speeding down here at a hell of a '''rate'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Clarendon History|passage=Many of the horse<!--SIC--> could not march at that '''rate''', nor come up soon enough.}}
# The relative speed of change or progress. {{defdate|from 18th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|The '''rate''' of production at the factory is skyrocketing.}}
# The price of (an individual) thing; [[cost]]. {{defdate|from 16th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|He asked quite a '''rate''' to take me to the airport.}}
# A set [[price]] or [[charge]] for all examples of a given case, commodity, service etc. {{defdate|from 16th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|Postal '''rates''' here are low.}}
# A [[wage]] calculated in relation to a unit of time.
#: {{ux|en|We pay an hourly '''rate''' of between $10 – $15 per hour depending on qualifications and experience.}}
# Any of various [[tax]]es, especially those levied by a local authority. {{defdate|from 17th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|I hardly have enough left every month to pay the '''rates'''.}}
# {{lb|en|nautical}} A [[class]] into which [[ship]]s were assigned based on condition, size etc.; by extension, [[rank]].
#: {{ux|en|This textbook is first-'''rate'''.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} Established portion or measure; fixed allowance; [[ration]].
#* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|book=IV|canto=VIII|passage=The one right feeble through the evil '''rate''' / Of food which in her duress she had found.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete|uncountable}} Order; arrangement.
#* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|book=IV|canto=X|passage=Thus sat they all around in seemly '''rate'''.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} Ratification; approval.
#* '''c. 1610s''', {{w|George Chapman}}, ''Caesar and Pompey''
# {{lb|en|horology}} The gain or loss of a timepiece in a unit of time.
#: {{ux|en|daily '''rate'''; hourly '''rate'''; etc.}}

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[assign]] or be assigned a particular [[rank]] or [[level]].
#: {{ux|en|She is '''rated''' fourth in the country.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[evaluate]] or [[estimate]] the [[value]] of.
#: {{syn|en|appraise|evaluate|worthen|Thesaurus:appraise}}
#: {{ux|en|They '''rate''' his talents highly.}}
#* '''1661''', {{w|Robert South}}, ''False Foundations Removed'' (sermon)
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[consider]] or [[regard]].
#: {{syn|en|esteem|regard|respect|Thesaurus:revere}}
#: {{ux|en|He '''rated''' this book brilliant.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[deserve]]; to be [[worth]].
#: {{ux|en|The view here hardly '''rates''' a mention in the travel guide.}}
#* '''1955''', [[w:Rex Stout|Rex Stout]], "When a Man Murders...",<!--... in title--> in [[w:Three Witnesses (book)|''Three Witnesses'']], October 1994 [[w:Bantam Books|Bantam]] edition, {{ISBN|0553249592}}, page 101:
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[determine]] the [[limit]]s of safe [[function]]ing for a [[machine]] or [[electrical]] [[device]].
#: {{ux|en|The transformer is '''rated''' at 10 watts.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|chiefly|British}} To [[evaluate]] a [[property]]'s [[value]] for the purposes of local [[taxation]].
# {{lb|en|transitive|informal}} To [[like]]; to think highly of.
#: {{ux|en|The customers don't '''rate''' the new burgers.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|horse racing}} To take action to slow down the pace of the horse one is riding.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2019|author=Jay Cronley|title=Good Vibes
|passage=Throughout the first turn is where the jockey '''rates''' the horse if the need arises. '''Rating''' a horse is where you keep it from putting out too much too soon.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To have [[position]] (in a certain [[class]]).
#: {{syn|en|rank}}
#: {{ux|en|She '''rates''' among the most excellent chefs in the world.}}
#: {{ux|en|He '''rates''' as the best cyclist in the country.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To have value or [[standing]].
#: {{ux|en|This last performance of hers didn't '''rate''' very high with the judges.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[ratify]].
#* {{RQ:Homer Chapman Iliads|year=1843|passage=to '''rate''' the truce}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[ascertain]] the exact rate of the gain or loss of (a [[chronometer]]) as compared with true [[time]].

===Etymology 2===
From {{der|en|enm|raten||to scold, chide}}, from {{der|en|non|hrata||to refuse, reject, slight, find fault with}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*hratōną||to sway, shake}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*krad-||to swing}}. Cognate with {{cog|sv|rata||to reject, refuse, find fault, slight}}, {{cog|no|rata||to reject, cast aside}}, {{cog|ang|hratian||to rush, hasten}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[berate]], [[scold]].
#* {{RQ:Tyndale NT|John|IX|text=Then '''rated''' they hym, and sayde: Thou arte hys disciple.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 6-3|act=II|scene=ii|passage=Go, '''rate''' thy minions, proud, insulting boy!}}
#* {{RQ:Montaigne Florio Essayes|chapter=56|book=I|passage=''Andronicus'' the Emperour, finding by chance in his pallace certaine principall men very earnestly disputing against ''Lapodius'' about one of our points of great importance, taunted and '''rated''' them very bitterly, and threatened if they gave not over, he would cause them to be cast into the river.}}
#* {{RQ:Bunyan Pilgrim's Progress|page=114|passage=So when he aroſe, he getteth him a grievous Crab-tree cudgel, and goes down into the ''Dungeon'' to them; and there firſt falls to '''Rateing''' of them, as if they were dogs: [...]}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=a. 1692|author=w:Isaac Barrow|title=The Danger and Mischief of Delaying Repentance
|passage=Conscience is a check to beginners in sin, reclaiming them from it, and '''rating''' them for it.}}
#* {{RQ:Scott Talisman|III|IV|pageref=103|pages=103–104|text=He beheld him, his head still muffled in the veil [...] couching, like a '''rated''' hound, upon the threshold of the chapel; but, apparently, without venturing to cross it: {{...}} a man borne down and crushed to the earth by the burden of his inward feelings.}}
#* {{RQ:Carlyle Past and Present|2|XV, Practical — Devotional||The successful monk, on the morrow morning, hastens home to Ely [...]. The successful monk, arriving at Ely, is '''rated''' for a goose and an owl; is ordered back to say that Elmset was the place meant.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1902|year_published=1980|author=w:Barbara Baynton|title=Bush Studies|series=Portable Australian Authors: Barbara Baynton|editors=Sally Krimmer; Alan Lawson|publisher=University of Queensland Press|location=St Lucia|page=71|passage=
Jyne took the baby, and began to '''rate''' the mother mildly for `walkin' seven mile ser soon', but Jyne's mother interposed with a recital of `wot I dun w'en Jun' (John) `wur two days old.'}}

{{trans-see|berate}}

===Etymology 3===
Related to, or a variant of, {{m|en|ret}}. (Found dialectally also as ''[[Citations:rait|rait]]''.)

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|UK|_|dialectal|obsolete}} To cause ([[hay]], [[hemp]], [[flax]], etc) to [[decay]] (whether in an [[injurious]] way, or—as [[ret]]ting—in a useful way) by exposure to [[weather]], particularly [[wetness]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1796|author=Mr. Marshall (William)|title=The Rural Economy of Yorkshire: Compromising the Management of Landed Estates and the Present Practice of Husbandry in the Agricultural Districts of that County|page=70
|text=From the "line pit" it [flax] is carried to the “'''RATING''' GROUND;" - a piece of unbroken aftergrass, where the sheaflets are untied, and the flax spread thin upon the grass. It is calculated, that a full crop ought to cover as much ground as it grew upon. Here it lies until it be sufficiently "'''rated''';" namely, until the more woodlike substance of the stems will separate {{...}} }}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1857|author=Henry Best|author2=Surtees Society (Durham, City of)|title=Rural Economy in Yorkshire in 1641, Being the Farming and Account Books of Henry Best, of Elmsworth, in the East Riding of the County of York|page=34
|text={{...}} hay when it is cocked either wette or greene, for then sure it is to be '''rated''', and beinge '''rated''' looseth both the goode smell and goode taste; and likewise the colour, as yow may perceive by the blackenesse of the cocke on the outside; for if the{{nb...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1889|author=Edward Peacock|title=A Glossary of Words Used in the Wapentakes of Manley and Corringham, Lincolnshire|page=433
|text="Frodingham of Roberte Westabie, for '''rateing''' hempe in Skinner Beck, contrairie to paine." - Kirton-in-Lindsey Fine Roll, 1630.}}
